The core operator 'build_unified_fantasy_and_dfs_dossier' integrates 10-Gate post-simulation projections with Morning Sweep data and live Sleeper trends. It synthesizes these inputs into a unified dossier containing Full/ Half/Standard PPR projections and VOR metrics. This enables consistent decision-making across fantasy and DFS domains by ensuring that both platforms rely on identical underlying data streams and computational logic. The VOR computation engine normalizes player projections into a common metric against replacement levels, allowing direct comparison across different scoring systems. The final tier assignment layer maps VOR and waiver trends into actionable fantasy start/sit and waiver priority labels. Dualities emerge in how the same data supports both long-term fantasy strategy and short-term DFS optimization. Failure modes include data drift from external sources, model misalignment in projection accuracy, or inconsistent application of 10-Gate filters. These are mitigated through cross-validation and telemetry checks.
